nodes.label: Check Reset Condition
nodes.description: Compare current_slot_timestamp against terminal_timestamp (genesis_time + period)

nodes.label: Reset Not Triggered
nodes.description: current_slot_timestamp < terminal_timestamp, continue normal operation

nodes.label: Reset Condition Met
nodes.description: current_slot_timestamp >= terminal_timestamp, begin reset sequence

nodes.description: Gracefully shutdown networking and consensus services

nodes.description: Store new genesis state in database

nodes.label: Restart Network Services

sub_graphs.title: EIP-6916: Validator Set Security
sub_graphs.description: Models the security boundaries around genesis validator set and takeover prevention

nodes.label: Genesis Validators Loaded
nodes.description: Initial validator set loaded at testnet start

nodes.label: Attacker Deposits Validators
nodes.description: Malicious actor adds validators to gain majority stake

nodes.label: Attacker Accumulating Stake
nodes.description: Attacker gradually increasing share of validator set

nodes.label: Calculate Time to 66% Majority
nodes.description: Based on validator count and activation rate, calculate epochs to majority

nodes.label: Takeover Timeline Determined
nodes.description: 10k validators = 5.7 days, 100k = 57.2 days, 200k = 114.5 days

nodes.label: Reset Occurs Before Takeover
nodes.description: Testnet resets clearing attacker progress if period < takeover time

nodes.label: Takeover Possible
nodes.description: Reset period exceeds takeover timeline - security risk

external_entities.name: Malicious Validator Operator
external_entities.description: Actor attempting to gain majority control of testnet validator set

ambiguities.text: The specification mentions reset periods should be 'relatively short (weeks/months)' without defining specific bounds.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume reset period should be chosen such that period < minimum_takeover_time for the genesis validator set size. For 10k validators, this means period < 5.7 days.

ambiguities.text: The behavior when a client fails to download the new genesis state from checkpoint sync endpoints is not specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume clients should retry with exponential backoff and fall back to generating genesis locally using hardcoded genesis_0 parameters.

ambiguities.text: The phrase 'sufficiently large genesis validator set' is used without quantification.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume minimum of 10,000 validators based on the security analysis table provided, giving ~5.7 days protection window.

implicit_assumptions.description: Checkpoint sync endpoints provide authentic genesis state data and are not compromised.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious genesis state could initialize nodes with attacker-controlled validator sets.

implicit_assumptions.description: All clients implementing EIP-6916 have synchronized clocks to accurately determine when reset condition is met.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Clock drift could cause network fragmentation as some nodes reset while others continue operating.

implicit_assumptions.description: The testnet infrastructure can handle periodic mass restarts without cascading failures.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Reset events could cause prolonged downtime if services fail to restart properly.

implicit_assumptions.description: The hardcoded genesis_0 parameters in client code are correct and have not been tampered with.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Incorrect genesis parameters would cause nodes to join incompatible networks.
